units.function: Broad database-backed host-service integration tests for plugin access to execution workspaces, issue orchestration, local folders, managed projects, checkout/wakeup, costs, human-attributed comments, interaction responses, approval decisions and attachment content.
units.dependencyDirection: A plugin worker calls privileged host services with plugin identity plus caller-supplied Company, Agent/run or user identifiers. Services mutate core issue/interaction/approval/project state, enqueue heartbeat work, read attachments/workspaces and write activity records over shared relational services.
units.keyDataModels: Plugin ID/key/origin namespace; Company/Agent/run/user/member role; execution workspace paths/provider metadata; issue/blocker/checkout/origin/billing/cost; local folder declaration; managed project; comment/wakeup request; interaction/action; approval/payload/decision; attachment/asset/size/hash.
units.lifecycle: Read a Company workspace; create and relate plugin-origin work; configure local data roots; reconcile a project; assert run ownership or request wakeup; summarize cost; write a human-attributed comment; resolve an interaction or approval; read bounded Company attachment content.
units.testAssessment: The 26 scenarios demonstrate meaningful tenant and operational safeguards: plugin origin namespaces, activity attribution, declared local-folder keys, blocker-aware wakeups, subtree cost filtering, viewer write denial, fail-closed missing actorUserId, idempotent already-resolved interactions, approval output redaction, Company-scoped attachments and size caps. All were skipped locally due unavailable embedded Postgres. The central identity test is insufficient: the plugin supplies a bare actorUserId and the host only rechecks active non-viewer membership, which does not prove the request came from that human. Capability enforcement is not exercised here, Agent/run spoof negatives are absent, workspace paths leak, project reconciliation is plugin-authoritative, approval action digests/evidence are absent, raw secret approval payload remains stored and comment wakeups are fire-and-forget with observable teardown races.
units.designRationale: Expose a rich but centralized host API so plugins can build orchestration and chat/control surfaces without direct database access, while attempting to preserve tenant, role, audit and redaction rules.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a narrow extension API that lets Chinese enterprise/FDE integrations act for authenticated humans and Agents without becoming a parallel control plane or accepting spoofable identity claims.
units.companyOsFit: REJECT the current human-attributed mutation contract based on caller-supplied user IDs, and do not expose the whole core orchestration surface to plugins. Define capability-specific commands with tenant/resource scopes. IdentityPort must mint or verify a short-lived delegation assertion bound to human principal, plugin audience, tenant, action, exact request digest, expiry and nonce; the plugin passes only that proof. Approval commands additionally bind work/contract/Agent/permissions/data/evidence/result digests and reviewer qualification. Verify Agent/run ownership server-side. Return opaque workspace/data handles, not host paths. Use transactional command/outbox events, idempotency keys and data-export policy. Retain origin namespaces, blocker checks, stable audit attribution, cost subtree filters and bounded attachment reads as reference patterns.
units.responsibilityConflict: An active non-viewer membership record is treated as sufficient proof that a plugin request came from that human. A compromised plugin can choose an owner/admin user ID and potentially comment, answer interactions or approve on their behalf. Approval rows are not shown bound to a responsibility contract, exact action, evidence or result digest, so the plugin surface can fabricate the human link in the responsibility chain.

2026-08-19 focused Vitest: file discovered; 26/26 tests skipped because embedded Postgres support was unavailable
units.securityFindings: CRITICAL human impersonation gap: plugin-supplied actorUserId is checked for membership/role but not cryptographically/session-bound to the requesting human. CRITICAL approval gap: privileged approval/interaction decisions lack delegated identity proof and exact action/responsibility/evidence digest binding. HIGH privilege-surface gap: capability denial and least-privilege method exposure are not exercised in this host-service suite. HIGH Agent attribution gap: negative Agent/run spoof tests are absent for plugin-created issues. HIGH data disclosure: absolute workspace paths/provider references reach plugins, and attachment reads lack tested data-contract/export policy. HIGH secret lifecycle gap: raw approval secret payload remains stored; output redaction appears key-pattern based and nested/novel fields are untested. MEDIUM durability gap: comment-triggered wake is fire-and-forget and requires global quiescence/retry cleanup. POSITIVE: tenant scoping, viewer denial, origin namespace, blocker wake guard, audit fields, redacted outputs and attachment size caps are explicitly tested. TEST GAP: all database-backed scenarios were skipped locally.
